evaluation_protocol.primary: test block, evaluated once after every choice was fixed
evaluation_protocol.validation: rolling-origin out-of-fold predictions over the validation block: each unit scored by a model fitted only on earlier units. They chose the hyperparameters, fitted the calibrators and set the thresholds, so metrics there are optimistic (selection) and calibration there is in-sample
evaluation_protocol.final_models: refitted on the whole development period (train and validation blocks) with the chosen settings; the calibrator fitted on out-of-fold scores is applied to them (Platt, 1999)
evaluation_protocol.label_use: test labels are masked in memory until the single final evaluation; the only earlier use is the count of test failures in the split rule (at least 15). Root cause, sensor health and FDC reference selection use development-period labels only

blocks.rule: units sorted by timestamp (unit id breaks ties), cuts only between different timestamps; test = last 20% of units; development period = everything before it; train = first 30% of the development period (rolling-origin warm-up, fitting only); validation = the rest of the development period (rolling-origin evaluation slices); a block start moves one timestamp at a time until every block holds at least 15 failures

boundaries.positions: 0-based positions in time order; a block starts at its position

plain_60_20_20_for_comparison.why_not_used: a single validation block this small holds too few failures to tune hyperparameters or fit a calibrator on; rolling-origin validation over the whole development period uses every failure after the warm-up instead

cross_validation.rule: expanding window over the development period; the train block (warm-up) is only fitted on; the validation block is cut into 5 consecutive slices of about equal size, each predicted by a model fitted on every earlier unit; slices with fewer than 5 failures are merged with a neighbour

split.leakage_check: passed: train < validation < test strictly in time, every unit in exactly one block, tied timestamps never split

tuning.objective: mean average precision over the rolling-origin folds

fixed.scale_pos_weight: passed / failed units in the fitting rows

logistic_regression.model: median imputation, standardisation, L2 logistic regression with balanced class weights (lbfgs)

comparisons.statistic: test PR-AUC of LightGBM minus PR-AUC of the baseline
comparisons.method: paired stratified bootstrap on the same resamples; two-sided p-value by percentile-interval inversion

difference.method: paired stratified bootstrap, 2000 resamples, percentile interval
paired stratified bootstrap, 2000 resamples, percentile interval
paired stratified bootstrap, 2000 resamples, percentile interval

calibration.method: Platt scaling (smoothed targets, Newton fit) on the pooled out-of-fold validation raw scores
calibration.prevalence_baseline: constant 0.0387, the validation-block failure rate (the data every calibrator was fitted on)
calibration.reliability_caveat: equal-count bins; with few failures per bin the observed rates are very uncertain (Wilson intervals shown)
calibration.isotonic_rejected: isotonic regression has up to one free level per distinct score and overfits a calibration set with few failures; its flat steps also tie units the model ranks differently

operating_points.thresholds_from: validation block: pooled out-of-fold LightGBM risks; the smallest threshold whose false-alarm rate there is at most the target

precision.method: stratified bootstrap, 2000 resamples, percentile interval, 2 resamples with undefined statistic excluded

operating_points.threshold_uncertainty: intervals are conditional on the thresholds chosen on the validation block

out_of_fold.note: validation-block risks come from the fold model whose evaluation slice holds them; train-block (warm-up) units have no out-of-sample risk

root_cause.importance: sum over members of mean |TreeSHAP| (log-odds) over development-period units, final model (fitted on the development period)

stability.resampling: stratified bootstrap of the development period; preprocessing fixed; one seed per refit

permutation_test.power_note: with 200 permutations the smallest p-value is 0.0050; Benjamini-Hochberg across 242 groups can declare k groups significant only if k >= 25 of them reach that floor

univariate.test: Mann-Whitney U, two-sided, failed versus passed development-period units, missing readings excluded; Benjamini-Hochberg across tested sensors

shap.sources: fold models for validation units; the final model (development period) for test units; train-block units have none

reference.rule: candidate references are the passing units within the first 50%, 40%, 30%, 20% of the development period (in time order); the longest stationary one is used

candidates.test: KPSS level-stationarity test (statsmodels, regression='c', automatic lags) on the first 5 principal-component scores, each at level 0.01 (Bonferroni, family level 0.05); statsmodels reports p-values only within [0.01, 0.10]

model.scaling: reference median imputation (FDC only); centred at the reference mean and scaled by the reference standard deviation, both after imputation
model.t2_limit_method: Phase II F limit for a new observation
model.spe_limit_method: Box chi-square approximation matched to the mean and variance of leave-one-out reference SPE (reference rows <= features)
model.contributions: SPE: squared residual per feature; T2: complete decomposition

small_shift_charts.group_score: sign-aligned mean of the members' FDC-standardised values, standardised by the fit-reference mean and SD

cusum.restart: both sums restart at zero after a signal

fdc.limitations: SECOM has no drift labels: these alarms cannot be scored as correct or incorrect, only checked for their false-alarm rate on held-out in-control data and for association with failure

failure_association.scope: all units outside the FDC reference stretch (later development units and the test block); association only, not causation

status: dead: never measured, or a single distinct value over the whole period

maintenance: a flatline window (at least 5 readings in a calendar week, all identical, with reference probability p_v ** n < 0.001); or a stuck value (a run of R >= 5 identical consecutive readings with n_readings * r ** (R - 1) < 0.01, r = the sensor's reference rate of repeating its previous reading, (repeats + 1) / (pairs + 2)); or a week missing at least 50% of readings while the reference misses at most 10%; or at least 20% of readings after the reference outside the reference range

watch: jumps (|robust z of a first difference| > 120.67, a threshold exceeded by 0.1% of reference differences) more frequent after the reference than the in-control share 0.100% allows (one-sided exact binomial test, Benjamini-Hochberg q <= 0.05); or a week missing at least 20% of readings while the reference misses at most 10%; or at least 5% of readings after the reference outside the reference range
rules.windows: ISO calendar weeks, Monday 00:00 to next Monday 00:00 (exclusive)
rules.reference: FDC reference fit set (earlier half of the stationary early stretch of passing development units); the later half is held out

jump.statistic: robust z of the first difference between consecutive readings: (d - median of reference differences) / (1.4826 x MAD of reference differences), per sensor
jump.calibration: smallest |z| exceeded by at most the target share of the first differences of the reference fit set, pooled over every sensor with a computable z

held_out_share_flagged.method: Clopper-Pearson exact interval (treats differences as independent)

rules.missing_vs_failure: Fisher exact test on the development period (test labels never used), Benjamini-Hochberg across testable sensors

limitations: Few failures: the test block holds 17 and the validation block 34, so every interval is wide and small differences between models are not distinguishable.
The failure rate drifts over time (see eda.md: many failures early, fewer later); a model and calibrator fitted on earlier periods may not transfer to later ones.
One fab, one product, about three months in 2008, anonymous sensors: results may not transfer to other tools, products or periods, and sensor meanings are unknown.
The source timestamps have no time zone; they are stored as UTC without conversion.
Associations, not causes: a sensor group linked to failure may be a proxy for another, unmeasured, factor.

Validation-block risks come from rolling-origin fold models fitted on less data than the final model; they chose the settings and the calibrator, so their metrics are optimistic. The calibrator is fitted on fold-model scores and applied to the final model, an approximation the test block checks.
Operating-point intervals are conditional on the thresholds chosen on the validation block; the variability of the threshold choice itself is not included.
The test-block curve in operating_points.json is descriptive; choosing a new threshold from it and reporting test performance at that threshold would be optimistic.
Reliability bins hold few failures each, so the observed rates are very uncertain.
with 200 permutations the smallest p-value is 0.0050; Benjamini-Hochberg across 242 groups can declare k groups significant only if k >= 25 of them reach that floor.
Stability selection uses bootstrap resamples (not the half-samples of Meinshausen and Buehlmann), so their error bound does not apply; stability is descriptive.

FDC has no drift labels in SECOM; alarms are judged only by their false-alarm rate on held-out in-control data and by association with failure. The PCA reference holds fewer units than sensors, so the covariance is estimated with few degrees of freedom.

Sensor-health rules are deterministic and label-free; the jump test treats consecutive differences as independent, which a single spike violates; the stuck-value rule uses a first-order repeat model fitted on a short reference; and 61 sensors already reach the out-of-reference watch rate on held-out in-control data, so that rule alone over-flags. Statuses are prompts for inspection, not diagnoses.
Missingness of sensor readings: 4 sensors associated with failure after Benjamini-Hochberg on the development period; reported as found, without searching for a test variant that would find more.
No candidate FDC reference passed the stationarity test; the shortest candidate is used.

fdc_reference.stationarity: KPSS level-stationarity test (statsmodels, regression='c', automatic lags) on the first 5 principal-component scores, each at level 0.01 (Bonferroni, family level 0.05); statsmodels reports p-values only within [0.01, 0.10]; no candidate stretch passed, so the shortest candidate is used and flagged as a limitation

methods.explanation: TreeSHAP from LightGBM (pred_contrib, exact for trees) in log-odds of the class-weighted model: validation units are explained by the rolling-origin fold model that scored them and test units by the final model refitted on the development period; each row's base value is its model's expected raw score.
methods.fdc: PCA on 106 passing reference units and 437 sensors (reference-median imputation, autoscaling to reference mean and SD), keeping 56 components (90.1% of variance); Hotelling T2 limits from the Phase II F distribution and SPE limits by Box chi-square approximation matched to the mean and variance of leave-one-out reference SPE (reference rows <= features), at 99% and 99.9%.
methods.contributions: SPE contributions are the squared residuals of each sensor (they sum to SPE); T2 contributions are the complete decomposition z_j (P Lambda^-1 t)_j, which sums to T2 and can be negative for a sensor that pulls the score back.
